analysis: **Public benchmark (D4).** This is our strongest result. On real failures in deployed systems, the rules control identified the correct service in 8 of 30 cases. With Qwen3.8 27B, our per-service summary reached 19 of 30 at Top-1 against 11 of 30 for a sample of raw lines (exact McNemar p = 0.039, uncorrected across the two models tested), and 26 of 30 against 19 of 30 at Top-3, while using 1,358 input tokens against 2,408. gpt-oss-120b moved in the same direction, 16 against 12 of 30 (p = 0.388). The summary design was fixed before RE3 was examined. A case holds far more log data than fits in a prompt, so the raw condition uses 40 evenly spaced lines while the summary draws on every line, which is precisely the advantage preprocessing provides. We will confirm this pilot on all 90 cases.

**Stakeholder logs (D3).** On the stakeholder's own 16 logs, for which the proposal published 16 of 16 with Claude Opus in both conditions, Qwen3.8 27B matched that result at 16 of 16. Accuracy rose with model capability, from 13 of 16 for gpt-oss-20b to 15 of 16 for gpt-oss-120b, which locates where smaller models become sufficient. The pipeline matched Baseline A's accuracy on every model while using 835 to 837 input tokens against 1,526 to 1,757. Our rebuilt parser reproduced the published summary for `pool_exhausted_run1` exactly, confirming the fidelity of the rebuild.

**Where the pipeline leads.** On D1 and D2, the pipeline matched or exceeded Baseline A on all six model and dataset combinations, using smaller models available on a free tier. On D1, which removes identifying error names and adds red herrings, Qwen3.8 27B reached 100% against 92.5% from raw logs. Deterministic preprocessing cut input tokens by about half at the same LLM call count, and all 236 pipeline answers were usable, against 231 of 236 for Baseline A. Each of these comparisons uses at most 40 paired logs, so we report them as directional results with exact p-values in Table 2.

**Where methods converge.** On D2, Qwen3.8 27B and gpt-oss-120b were 100% accurate in both LLM conditions across all 40 pairs, matching the 100% the proposal reported with Claude Opus on its own logs; Opus was not run on D2, so this is an indirect comparison. gpt-oss-20b reached 100% with the pipeline and 95% with Baseline A. Calibration varied by model: Brier score improved markedly for Qwen3.8 27B (0.065 to 0.002), held steady for gpt-oss-120b (0.050 to 0.048), and moved from 0.028 to 0.048 for gpt-oss-20b.

**Where the next gains are.** The rules control reached 100% on D1 to D3, confirming that those datasets provide clean, well-separated ground truth and motivating the harder D4 benchmark, where the summary clearly leads the rules. Red-herring handling is the most valuable refinement: gpt-oss-120b raised 2 false alarms on D1 in both conditions, and gpt-oss-20b raised 2 with the pipeline where Baseline A raised none, although Baseline A returned empty answers on 2 other `no_fault` logs.

**Why the design works.** The largest gains came with Qwen3.8 27B, whose Baseline A misses on D1 included 2 `dependency_down` logs read as `pool_exhausted`, the distinction the spacing fields make explicit. On D4, the summary gives each model a view of the whole incident that no prompt-sized sample of raw lines can provide. These findings point to structured preprocessing as a practical way to get more from smaller models.

**Evaluation scope.** D1 includes 36 of 40 pairs for gpt-oss-120b, with D2 complete at 40 pairs per model and D3 at 16. Hand review of runs flagged by the evidence rules on a partial D2 run found correct explanations, so the Proposal and Grounded columns can understate performance, and measuring the rules' sensitivity is planned. **Planned extensions:** longer-log sweeps, a parser without spacing fields, a live Claude run, a recovery sweep, and the remaining 60 RE3 cases.
